title: bdk.toml
description: BDK application configuration. The single source of truth for BDK-specific settings; the CLI validates it and writes bdk.resolved.json. See docs/planning/sdk/configuration.md.

pathString.description: A path relative to the directory of bdk.toml, with forward slashes, that stays inside it.

surfaceModeDefaultCustom.description: The surface allows the default presenter or a custom handler. It cannot be disabled.

surfaceModeAny.description: default: the default presenter unless a handler takes over. custom: a handler is required before start. disabled: the feature is unavailable.

endpoint.description: Optional. Keeps the provider's protocol and sends requests to this URL.

browser.description: Identity of the browser: its display name and branded internal URL scheme.

name.description: Display name. Used in default-presenter text and as the fallback for the identifiers derived from it.

internal_scheme.description: The branded internal URL scheme, for example cove for cove://settings. Lower case, matches [a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*, not a reserved scheme. Set it explicitly: a scheme derived from the name changes when the name does.

runtime.description: Which Chromium runtime the application uses and how profiles survive upgrades.

mode.description: prebuilt uses the published runtime for the resolved BDK version. source builds one from the checkout with the application's patches.

downgrade.description: What happens when an older engine meets a profile last used by a newer one and no snapshot exists. refuse fails start; fresh-profile starts with a new profile and leaves the old one untouched.

snapshot_on_upgrade.description: Snapshot each profile before the first launch of a newer engine milestone.

chromium.description: Chromium build inputs. Source only: every key here is an error when runtime.mode is prebuilt.

revision.description: A Chromium tag. Source only. Defaults to the pin of the resolved BDK version, and must be one the BDK version declares compatible.

patches.description: Source only. A directory with a series file, or an ordered list of patch files, applied after BDK's own series. Defaults to Chromium/patches if it exists.

gn_args.description: Source only. Extra GN arguments. Arguments on the deny list (sandbox, remote debugging, web security, Google API keys, sign-in and sync, auto-granted permissions) are rejected.

additionalProperties.description: The value of one GN argument.

pages.description: Internal pages: discovery, per-route overrides, aliases and capability grants.

auto_discover.description: Treat each directory under pages.directory that has an index.html as a page.

overrides.description: One line per logical route: route = mode. chromium serves the built-in page, native delivers the navigation to a Swift handler, disabled blocks it, and a path serves the bundled page at that path.

additionalProperties.description: chromium, native, disabled, or a path to a directory that contains index.html.

routes.description: One line per alias: alias = target. The target must be a page, never another alias. The alias shares the target's identity and capabilities.

additionalProperties.description: The logical route the alias points at.

capabilities.description: Capability grants, one table per bundled route: [pages.capabilities.<route>]. A page with no table has no capability.

allow.description: The BDK capabilities this page may use. A trailing * is allowed only after app., for example app.sidebar.*.

items.description: A capability name such as settings.read.

ui.description: Browser-owned UI surfaces and who presents them.

default_browser_surfaces.description: The mode for every surface not listed under [ui.surfaces]: true means default, false means custom.

surfaces.description: One line per surface: surface = default, custom or disabled. Which modes a surface allows is in ui-requests.md section 4.

new_windows.description: Popups, undocked DevTools, picture-in-picture and extension windows.

passwords.description: Save, update and generate password prompts.

autofill.description: Save address or card; fill confirmation.

autofill_suggestions.description: The suggestion list under a form field. Cannot be disabled; a disabled autofill surface turns it off.

printing.description: Print preview and the system print dialog.

translation.description: Translation offer, progress, result, errors and preferences.

exclusive_access.description: Keyboard-lock and pointer-lock notices. Cannot be disabled.

reputation_warnings.description: Malware, phishing and download warnings. Cannot be disabled.

device_choosers.description: WebUSB, Web Bluetooth, WebHID and Web Serial device choosers.

external_protocols.description: Opening a link in another application.

page_health.description: An unresponsive page; blocked popups. Cannot be disabled.

web_app_installs.description: The install prompt of an installable web app. Turn installs off with [web_apps] enabled = false, not here.

enabled.description: Whether a page may offer itself for installation and the webApps commands work. Push messages are [services.push].

extensions.description: The extension system: whether it exists, how extensions install and which UI surfaces present them.

enabled.description: The extension system as a whole. false removes extension APIs, pages and installation.

install_policy.description: Whether a manifest that requires a disabled or unsupported surface is refused before installation. With allow_all it installs, and unsupported calls still fail explicitly.

allow_in_private.description: Whether the user may allow an extension in private profiles.

developer_mode.description: Whether loading unpacked extensions is a user setting, always on, or unavailable.

crx.description: Install a local CRX file. BDK owns the off-store policy and keeps Chromium's install prompt.

update_urls.description: Which self-hosted update manifests an extension may name: any, or an array of URL patterns.

stores.description: Named store sources. chrome-web-store is available and off unless listed.

items.description: A store BDK ships an adapter for.

blocklist.description: Extension identifiers that never install or load, from any source.

items.description: An extension identifier: 32 letters from a to p.

bundled.description: Extensions shipped inside the application bundle: name = "Extensions/<directory>", or a table with path and required. They load with no prompt in every persistent profile and cannot be uninstalled.

additionalProperties.description: The extension's directory, a path relative to the directory of bdk.toml that the build copies into Contents/Resources; or a table with path and required.

ui.description: One line per extension surface, with the same three modes as [ui.surfaces]. Details are in extensions.md section 4.

services.description: Provider choice for each service. A flag is not a credential: choosing a provider never implies that its keys exist.

provider.description: default is the local engine, app is a Swift registration. The named providers arrive after v1.

models.description: Whether language models download when first needed or ship in the bundle.

bundled_languages.description: With models = bundled, which language pairs to include.

items.description: A language code such as en or pt-BR.

provider.description: default is the signed static block lists, app is a Swift registration.

update_interval.description: How often list updates are fetched, for list-based providers. A duration such as 30m, 1h or 1d.

provider.description: system is the operating system's provider, app is a Swift registration.

webauthn.description: Passkeys and security keys. Not a provider table: WebAuthn has no provider to choose.

phones.description: Whether a passkey on a phone (QR code, Bluetooth, the phone's tunnel service) is offered. Off by default because an Android phone's tunnel service is a Google host; on also needs NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription.

push.description: Web Push, for any site that subscribes, installed as a web app or not.

provider.description: none: pages have no Push API and no messaging host is contacted. google: Google's messaging service, through Chromium's own push client, which registers with Google as Chrome does; it needs no Google project or key.

automation.description: The automation host and application-authored scripts.

enabled.description: Whether the automation host exists in this application.

directory.description: Where application-authored scripts live. Each top-level .ts or .js file is one script.

cpu_budget_ms.description: The CPU time in milliseconds one task's script may use before the automation host stops it. Not wall-clock time: a script waiting on a command costs nothing.

external.description: The authenticated local endpoint. There is no key for a network port.

enabled.description: Whether the application may open the authenticated local endpoint at runtime. true only permits it; Swift opens it.

devtools.description: The DevTools front end and protocol.

frontend.description: default (Chromium's front end), disabled (none), or a path to a complete replacement packaged from that directory.

overlay.description: A directory of CSS and JavaScript loaded into the default front end.

protocol.description: Whether the DevTools protocol is available to Swift and to automation sessions that hold contents.debug. Independent of the front end.

typescript.description: Generate @bdk/* declarations. Defaults to true when Pages/ or Automation/ exists.

commands_module.description: The Swift module whose command, event and setting declarations are extracted. Defaults to the application target.
